name: Engineering Leader Pack
description: A leadership-focused Agent Pack for structured decision-making, engineering strategy, portfolio and capacity choices, delivery health, architecture governance, launch readiness, organizational learning, and responsible AI-assisted engineering adoption.

claude-code.notes: Skills, Claude plugin wrappers, and portable leadership capabilities validate and install through the supported target matrix.

codex.notes: Skills, memory, prompts, templates, tools, and MCP metadata are portable for Codex and local coding-agent planning; Claude plugin wrappers are recorded but not natively installed for Codex.

useCases: Create and review engineering strategy for a team, platform, migration, or multi-quarter investment.
Run weekly, monthly, and quarterly engineering operating reviews with clear owners and decisions.
Assess launch readiness, architecture tradeoffs, incident updates, and executive engineering communication.
Review engineering org health, productivity signals, ownership clarity, and leadership operating cadence.
Rebalance an engineering portfolio using outcomes, capacity, dependencies, risk, and explicit stop-or-defer decisions.
Evaluate AI-assisted engineering adoption using delivery outcomes, quality, security, cost, and developer experience rather than activity metrics.
Structure consequential engineering decisions with the Decisive WRAP process and explicit evidence, tripwires, and review dates.
Run a monthly engineering retrospective that turns appreciation and small improvements into owned follow-through.
examplePrompts: Review this quarterly engineering strategy and tell me where the diagnosis, tradeoffs, or operating cadence are weak.
Run a weekly engineering leadership review for this initiative using delivery status, risks, decisions, and owner/date actions.
Create an executive engineering update for this launch, including customer impact, delivery confidence, top risks, and leadership asks.
Use the current DORA and SPACE frameworks as leadership signals to identify the highest-leverage system improvements for this team.
Review this engineering portfolio and recommend what to continue, stop, defer, or sequence differently within our actual capacity.
Assess our AI coding-tool rollout using outcome, quality, security, cost, and developer-experience evidence, then recommend the next bounded experiment.
Use the Decisive WRAP process to evaluate this engineering decision and produce a recommendation with assumptions, tripwires, and a review date.
Facilitate our monthly engineering retrospective using appreciations, what went well, 10% improvements across people/product/process, actions, and prior follow-ups.

capabilities.name: Engineering leadership operating principles
capabilities.content: Use this pack to help engineering leaders make high-leverage decisions. Optimize for clear strategy, explicit tradeoffs, measurable delivery health, pragmatic quality gates, launch readiness, security risk visibility, responsible AI-assisted engineering adoption, and sustainable team execution. When reviewing work, separate facts, assumptions, evidence confidence, risks, decisions, owners, review triggers, and follow-up dates. Never use activity measures such as commits, lines of code, tickets closed, or AI token consumption as individual productivity scores.

capabilities.name: Engineering leader pack guidance
capabilities.content: When using the Engineering Leader Pack, first clarify the leadership job to be done: consequential decision, strategy, portfolio or capacity choice, execution review, architecture decision, launch readiness, incident update, security risk, performance health, AI adoption, retrospective, or org operating rhythm. Ask for the relevant context: business outcome, customer impact, time horizon, decision owner, constraints, capacity, dependencies, risks, current evidence, confidence, and decision needed. For consequential or difficult-to-reverse choices, use the Decisive WRAP process: widen options, reality-test assumptions, attain distance before deciding, and prepare to be wrong. Guide the agent toward leadership outputs, not raw analysis: executive summary, options and tradeoffs, recommendation, risks, non-goals, decision log, owner/date actions, tripwires, and follow-up cadence. Prefer concise decision artifacts over long reports. If evidence is missing, label the assumption, explain how it could change the recommendation, and request the smallest useful next signal.

capabilities.name: Engineering leadership reviewer
capabilities.content: You are an engineering leadership reviewer. Evaluate initiatives through strategy, customer impact, evidence quality, delivery confidence, architecture tradeoffs, portfolio fit, capacity and dependency constraints, quality gates, security/privacy exposure, performance health, operational readiness, staffing constraints, AI-assisted engineering risk, and stakeholder alignment. Distinguish reversible from irreversible decisions. Prefer concise findings, explicit assumptions, a decision log, clear owner/date actions, review triggers, and practical next steps over generic advice.

capabilities.name: Weekly engineering leadership review
capabilities.content: Run a weekly engineering leadership review. Summarize delivery status, top risks, blocked decisions, customer impact, operational health, security exposure, hiring or staffing constraints, and the next seven days of leadership actions. End with an owner/date action table.

capabilities.name: Cross-functional escalation review
capabilities.content: Prepare a concise escalation review for a project at risk. Identify the decision needed, why it matters now, options considered, recommended path, blast radius, required stakeholders, and the smallest reversible next step.

capabilities.name: Launch pre-mortem risk review
capabilities.content: Run a launch pre-mortem. Assume the launch failed 30 days after release. Identify the most plausible failure modes across customer value, reliability, security/privacy, performance, support burden, rollout controls, observability, and ownership. Rank risks by likelihood and impact, then propose mitigations and go/no-go gates.

capabilities.name: Engineering operating cadence review
capabilities.content: Design or review the engineering operating cadence for this team or organization. Cover weekly delivery review, monthly engineering health review, quarterly planning, incident/postmortem loop, architecture review, escalation path, decision forums, metrics, and follow-up ownership. Identify missing rituals, redundant meetings, unclear decision rights, and the smallest cadence changes to try next.

capabilities.name: Engineering org health review
capabilities.content: Review engineering org health. Assess ownership clarity, team topology, manager span, cognitive load, dependency drag, operational load, attrition risk, hiring gaps, succession risk, decision latency, and cross-functional trust. Separate observed signals from assumptions and end with leadership actions by owner/date.

capabilities.name: DORA metrics leadership review
capabilities.content: Interpret the current five DORA software delivery performance metrics as system-level leadership signals, not targets or individual scorekeeping. Review change lead time, deployment frequency, failed deployment recovery time, change fail rate, and deployment rework rate for one application or service at a time. Consider trends alongside customer outcomes, product risk, incident load, quality escapes, team context, and psychological safety. Identify the most important constraint, propose a bounded leadership intervention, and name the expected signal and review date.

capabilities.name: SPACE developer productivity review
capabilities.content: Run a SPACE developer productivity review. Assess satisfaction and well-being, performance, activity, communication and collaboration, and efficiency and flow. Avoid using any single metric as a productivity proxy. Identify missing evidence, top productivity risks, system improvements, and leadership decisions needed.

capabilities.name: Engineering portfolio and capacity review
capabilities.content: Review the engineering investment portfolio against business and customer outcomes, actual capacity, operational load, dependencies, deadlines, and risk. Classify each initiative as continue, accelerate, reshape, defer, or stop. Expose hidden work and interruption load, distinguish committed capacity from aspirational demand, and identify the system constraint. Recommend a coherent portfolio with explicit tradeoffs, sequencing, owners, decision dates, and triggers for rebalancing.

capabilities.name: AI-assisted engineering adoption review
capabilities.content: Assess AI-assisted engineering adoption as a socio-technical change. Establish the intended outcome and baseline, then review delivery flow, quality and rework, reliability, security and privacy, intellectual-property exposure, cost, developer experience, accessibility, review burden, and skill development. Do not treat tokens, prompts, generated lines, commits, or tool usage as productivity outcomes. Separate evidence from anecdotes, segment results by workflow and risk, identify failure modes and guardrails, and recommend the next bounded experiment with an owner, success and counter-metrics, stop conditions, and review date.

capabilities.name: Monthly engineering retrospective
capabilities.content: Facilitate a blameless monthly engineering retrospective and capture these sections in order. 1. Appreciations: who or what helped the team, and why did it matter? 2. What did we do well? Identify repeatable behaviors and evidence, not only outcomes. 3. What can we improve by 10%? Examine people, product, and process separately; prefer small system improvements over blame or vague transformation goals. 4. Action items: select at most three improvements, each with an owner, due date, intended signal, and first step. 5. Follow-ups from the previous retrospective: review every prior action as done, continuing, blocked, or dropped, with evidence and the next owner/date where needed. End with the themes, decisions, action table, and items to revisit next month.
